digest.definition: A family of separate but closely related land-based and food subjects, each a subject in its own right, running from field to fork
distinctiveFeatures: A family of separate but closely related land-based and food subjects, each a subject in its own right, running from field to fork
Its context is economic and social: the subjects bear on global sustainability, and graduates make evidence-informed decisions from international policy down to local practice
Sustainability is a priority, taken holistically and through approaches such as One Health that link people, animals, plants and environment

Agriculture covers farming systems, crop and animal production, natural resources and farm economics; horticulture covers plant science, production systems and landscapes; forestry covers woodland and forest management for market and wider benefits
Rural environmental sciences treat the countryside as a complex environmental and cultural resource, multidisciplinary and analytical
Animal studies concern the husbandry, welfare and management of non-production animals and a good life for them
Food science, food technology, human nutrition and consumer science span the food supply chain, safe and sustainable food, health and how consumer choices are made and changed
The subjects are practical: field observation, empirical data, laboratory and field work and work-based learning are central

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: inclusive access, recruitment and support across the student journey, with attention to the hidden curriculum, rural and disadvantaged students, equitable work-based learning, gender equity in horticulture and unequal consumer access (D1, 1.5 to 1.10; 2.1; 2.2; 3.10; 3.12; 4.2)

inclusive design and risk assessment for practical and field activities, reasonable adjustments to fieldwork and assessment, and the digital divide in blended learning (D1, 1.11, 1.12; 3.10; 3.17; 3.21)

sustainability runs through every grouping: sustainable production, net zero on farms, circular economies, sustainable forest and rural management and a resilient food supply; the SDGs and One Health frame it (D1, 1.13 to 1.16; 2.4 to 2.10; 3.24; 4.2)
enterprise and employability through placements, start-ups, accrediting bodies and authentic assessment, with employer expectations set out for each grouping (D1, 1.17 to 1.22; 3.17; 3.19; 3.20)
generative AI analysed for its effect on the agri-food supply chain and used reflectively and transparently (D1, 1.23; 4.3)
